One edge each pairs the nodes into three separate edges; one triangle each groups them into two triangles; and one of each gives two triangles plus three more edges, two of which happen to repeat a triangle side and are drawn bowed apart." width="100%"} Newman's clustered configuration model. Node `i` is given `(s, t)` from `joint_degree_sequence[i]`: `s` stubs for single edges and `t` corners of triangles. The edge stubs are shuffled and joined in pairs, and the triangle corners are shuffled and joined in triples, each triple becoming a triangle. Node `i` therefore ends with degree `s + 2 * t`, and unlike the plain configuration model the graph has plenty of triangles, so its clustering can be tuned. As in the configuration model, stubs are paired blindly, so self-loops and parallel edges can appear (`simplify()` removes them). The process is NetworkX's `random_clustered_graph()`. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Random clustered graphs are useful for: - null models that keep both the degrees and the triangle counts of a network - studying how clustering changes percolation and epidemic thresholds, which have exact solutions for this model - generating test networks with a chosen clustering coefficient ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [joint_degree_sequence]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One `(s, t)` pair of non-negative integers per node: its number of single-edge stubs and of triangle corners. The `s` values must sum to an even number and the `t` values to a multiple of `3`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an entry is negative, the single-edge stubs sum to an odd number, or the triangle corners don't sum to a multiple of `3`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Sixty nodes, each with one single edge and two triangle corners, so degree `4`: ::: {#0c66b23c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_random_clustered_graph([(1, 2)] * 60, seed=7) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), sum(graph.count_triangles().values()) // 3 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (60, 150, 45) ``` ::: ::: The planted triangles give a high clustering coefficient, which a configuration model with the same degrees lacks: ::: {#904a2f6f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} plain = ec.Graph().configuration_model([4] * 60, seed=7) round(graph.transitivity(), 2), round(plain.transitivity(), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.25, 0.03) ``` ::: :::
